column1: # The refused number-token vectors (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §16.2, docs/rulings.json
# json-wide-integers-refuse-number-token). The unit and root are MANIFEST.tsv's:
# `Integers`, unchanged.
# The rule: an integer field whose kind is wider than 32 bits takes the STRING
# form only; a bare number token there refuses kind_mismatch. Each row writes
# one wide field of Integers (or, for `numbers`, every wide field) as a bare
# number token, with every other field canonical. Each row has a string twin, a
# read vector in MANIFEST.tsv that holds the same values as strings and reads
# to them. Narrow integers (32 bits and under) stay JSON numbers everywhere.
# This is a separate manifest from MANIFEST.tsv because the readers are being
# moved to it one leg at a time: a leg's test reads these rows once that leg
# refuses a bare number token in a wide field.
# Kinds the Integers unit does not hold — uint128, bits(33..64), and the
# 128-bit fixed kinds — get no row here; the engine's own unit tests cover
# them.
# Columns, tab-separated: name, root, json file, verdict, what it holds.
wide-number
column5: the int64 as a bare number; string twin canonical.read.json

column1: uwide-number
column5: the uint64 as a bare number; string twin canonical.read.json

column1: wide128-number
column5: the ranged int128 as a bare number; string twin canonical.read.json

column1: ranged-number

column1: frac-number

column1: numbers
column5: every wide field as a bare number; string twin strings.read.json
